label: Sie
notes: The base rows: Sie with the third-person plural verb, as to any adult stranger.

label: du
notes: du with the second-person singular verb and imperative, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; ihr, its plural, where a question is put to a whole shop, restaurant or house (Habt ihr einen Tisch frei?). e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: vous
notes: The base rows: vous with the second-person plural verb, as to any adult stranger.

label: tu
notes: tu with the second-person singular verb and imperative and s'il te plaît, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; a question put to a whole shop or restaurant keeps vous, which is the plural of tu too. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: usted
notes: The base rows: usted with the third-person singular verb, as to any adult stranger.

label: tú
notes: tú with the second-person singular verb and imperative, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller (tuteo; regional vos is not written). The plural stays ustedes, which is the familiar plural too in the Latin-American Spanish of these rows. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: вы
notes: The base rows: вы with the second-person plural verb, as to any adult stranger.

label: ты
notes: ты with the second-person singular verb and imperative, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller. A ты past tense or short adjective agrees with the listener's gender, which this axis does not ask, so such sentences keep their base row or take an ungendered wording. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: 해요
notes: The base rows: 해요체 (합쇼체 in set phrases such as 감사합니다), with the honorific -시- toward the listener, as to any adult stranger.

label: 해
notes: 해체 (반말): the -요 dropped, and the honorific -시- with it, to a child or a friend of one's own age. Korean marks the hearer in every sentence ending, so this covers sentences about the speaker too. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: Lei
notes: The base rows: Lei with the third-person singular verb, and the subjunctive for a request (Si fermi, Mi dica), as to any adult stranger.

label: tu
notes: tu with the second-person singular verb and imperative (Fermati, Dimmi, Non usare), to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; a question put to a whole shop, restaurant or hotel keeps voi (Avete...?), which is the plural of tu too. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: você
notes: The base rows: the third-person singular verb with the pronoun left out, as one addresses o senhor, a senhora or você -- any adult stranger, in Portugal and in Brazil alike.

label: tu
notes: tu with the second-person singular verb and imperative (Para aqui, Diz-me, Não uses), the European familiar address, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller. The Brazilian text_alt is inherited unchanged, since in Brazil você with the third-person verb is itself the familiar address; a question put to a whole hotel keeps the plural (Têm...?, Podem...?), which is the same in both registers. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: です
notes: The base rows: 丁寧体 (です・ます体), the 丁寧語 です and ます closing every sentence, as to any adult stranger.

label: だ
notes: 普通体 (だ体): です becomes だ and ます the dictionary form, a question is asked with a rise and no か, ください becomes the bare て form, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller. Japanese marks the hearer in every sentence ending, so this covers sentences about the speaker too; the casual first person and the gendered sentence-final particles are left out. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: siz
notes: The base rows: siz with the second-person plural verb, imperative (-in, -yin) and possessive (-iniz), as to any adult stranger.

label: sen
notes: sen with the second-person singular verb, the bare-stem imperative and the singular possessive (-in), to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; siz is also the plural of sen, so a question put to a whole hotel (Boş odanız var mı?) does not change. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: आप
notes: The base rows: आप with the plural verb and the -इए imperative (दीजिए, बोलिए), as to any adult stranger.

label: तुम
notes: तुम with the -ओ imperative (दो, बोलो) and तुम्हारा, तुम्हें, to a friend of one's own age, a child or a fellow traveller; तू, intimate or rude to a stranger, is never written. Only second-person forms change. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: آپ
notes: The base rows: آپ with the plural verb and the -یے imperative (دیجیے, بولیے), as to any adult stranger.

label: تم
notes: تم with the -و imperative (دو, بولو) and تمہارا, تمہیں, to a friend of one's own age, a child or a fellow traveller; تو, intimate or rude to a stranger, is never written. Only second-person forms change. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.
